changes: Optional BREDITOR_PERF_OWNER_REPETITIONS=3..100 changes only the disposable performance fixture owner-loop bound. Nondefault values require queue diagnostics. Exact correctness assertions, disposal and between-owner task yields remain. Expected case counts and odd/even medians now derive from the configured count; the default remains three.

Optional BREDITOR_PERF_EXCEPTION_PROBE=1 installs a page-only init script for WebKit full-editor mode, mutually exclusive with catch-site/profiling/export diagnostics. It wraps construction through global Error, TypeError and RangeError while leaving application bundle bytes unchanged. Retains at most 32 records, 1024-character messages and 4096-character stacks, plus a dropped count. No document snapshots, engine handles or arbitrary thrown payload serialization.

Probe capture copies application records before a constructed-and-caught TypeError positive control after fixture completion/failure. Control success is mandatory and recorded separately. It does not inject a command, alter failure recovery or clear the original fault.
limits: The constructor probe changes the page environment and constructor identities even though application bundle bytes remain identical. It is diagnostic evidence, not a performance benchmark.
It observes global constructor calls with new, not every engine-originated exception, arbitrary thrown value or Error call without new. Empty records do not prove that no exception was caught.
Same-page owner churn is a distinct hypothesis from repeated fresh browsers and not a reliable reproducer yet. The 300-case pass does not rule out warm-up/allocation-sensitive behavior.
All retained stacks are local synthetic-fixture diagnostics; inspect before sharing. No production logging or browser settings were changed.
verification: 21 tests pass: five queue/owner-loop diagnostic tests, three isolated-realm constructor-probe tests, seven Gecko-profile summary tests and six rendering-trace summary tests.
Six invalid diagnostic/count combinations reject before artifact reads or fixture staging.
Source syntax and git diff checks pass.
Same-page stress completed 100 owners per size (300 exact-state cases); every recorded metric median was independently recomputed from its 100 sorted samples.

Ten constructor-probed browser runs completed 90 exact-state cases with zero constructor records or drops. The final positive-control implementation completed another nine cases and verified the expected caught TypeError.

Both constructor-probe JS/Wasm bundle asset maps exactly match the original failed uninstrumented artifact. The positive control is after capture, so it is excluded from application exception records.

Default, uninstrumented, three-owner mode completed 27 cases across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit after the runner changes. This qualifies the default runner path, not resolution of the original fault.
conclusion: No recurrence in these runs and no captured underlying exception. The original fault remains unresolved and the Rust candidate remains private/unpromoted. New tools make longer same-page testing and exact-bundle exception capture reproducible; they do not establish a WebKit or Rust root cause. A useful next comparison is the retained uninstrumented fixture in native Safari versus bundled WebKit, without changing Mac input or accessibility settings.
remaining: Full beta goal stays active: responsiveness, intermittent WebKit failure, native IME/VoiceOver evidence, delivery/size policy and full release qualification remain open. No version change, shipping rebuild, push or publish.
